Title: PRE-FLIGHT -- Returns Module Installed, Return Setting On, return-attachments Upload Scope Configured (Suite BLOCKED, Not FAIL, When Any Is Missing)
Preconditions:
Runner-native. No browser. Nothing is created except one unattached probe file. ENVIRONMENT REQUIRED BY THIS SUITE (a miss here makes the suite BLOCKED, never FAIL):
(1) Module VirtoCommerce.Return installed (GET /api/platform/modules, isInstalled=true).
(2) Store {{STORE_ID}} Settings > Return > Return: "Return module" (Return.ReturnEnabled) = ON; "Order statuses allowing returns" (Return.AllowedOrderStatuses) contains Completed; "Return window, days" (Return.WindowDays) = 30; "Photos or documents required" (Return.AttachmentsRequired) = ON (the create cases attach one file per line); "Return reasons" (Return.Reasons) contains NoLongerNeeded.
(3) Platform configuration FileUpload:Scopes includes return-attachments (without it POST /api/files/return-attachments is refused and every create case cannot attach).
(4) Seeded fixtures: npm run seed:returns (RETURNS_ORDER_*) and npm run seed:returns:decisions (RETURNS_AUTH_JOURNEY) — check with npm run returns:check / npm run returns:decisions:check; buyer {{USER_EMAIL}} and agent {{ADMIN}} (holds return:authorize); colleague {{USER2_EMAIL}} in the SAME organization (RETURNS_COLLEAGUE).
Steps:
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT]
[REST-OP modules]
GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules
[REST-EXEC modules]
[AUTH role=USER]
[GQL-OP policy]
query { returnPolicy(storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}") { isEnabled windowDays allowedOrderStatuses } }
[GQL-EXEC policy]
[REST-OP upload_probe]
POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/files/return-attachments
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
Body: file=@@td(UPLOAD_FIXTURES.primary.path) (mimeType: image/png; filename: Logo1.png)
[REST-EXEC upload_probe]
[REST-CAPTURE upload_probe.body.[0].url → PROBE_URL]
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=modules] HTTP 200
[DATA label=modules] body.[?title=Returns].isInstalled = true
[ERRORS label=policy] errors[] empty
[DATA label=policy] data.returnPolicy.isEnabled = true
[ERRORS label=upload_probe] HTTP 200
[DATA label=upload_probe] body.[0].url is non-null
[EVIDENCE] BLOCKED guard: every assertion in this case is an ENVIRONMENT prerequisite. A failure here means the stand is not prepared (module absent, store Return module setting off, FileUpload:Scopes without return-attachments) and the whole suite must be reported BLOCKED with the failing prerequisite named - it is not a product FAIL and no later case in this suite is meaningful.
Cross_Layer_Checks: [REST] evidence is the graphql-runner JSON per label; the probe file is left unattached (no return references it)
Failure_Signals: modules does not list VirtoCommerce.Return as installed; returnPolicy.isEnabled=false (Settings > Return > Return > "Return module" is off for the store); the upload probe is refused (platform FileUpload:Scopes lacks return-attachments) - each means SUITE BLOCKED, environment to be fixed, not a defect
Cleanup: none -- the probe upload is unreferenced
References: VCST-5628 · VCST-5883 · Archetype:CONFIG · Technique:EG | Promoted: VCST-5628 (2026-10-01)

Attachment provided up front (Return.AttachmentsRequired is true on this store) so the submit step exercises quantity logic, not the attachment gate (RET-GQL-018 covers that gate on its own).
Steps:
[AUTH role=USER]
[GQL-OP before]
query { returnableItems(orderId: "@td(RETURNS_ORDER_A2_PARTIAL_DELIVERY.id)") { orderLineItemId returnableQuantity } }
[GQL-EXEC before]
[GQL-CAPTURE before.data.returnableItems.0.returnableQuantity → BEFORE_QTY]
[REST-OP upload_att]

Body: file=@@td(UPLOAD_FIXTURES.primary.path) (mimeType: image/png; filename: Logo1.png)

[ERRORS label=after_submit] errors[] empty

RET-GQL-015 pinned only that a Draft's number is non-null against the DEFAULT template (RET{0:yyMMdd}-{1:D5}), which cannot tell a working template setting from a hardcoded RET-prefixed generator. This case changes Return.ReturnNewNumberTemplate to QATEST{0:yyMMdd}-{1:D5}, creates a throwaway Draft on fixture RETURNS_ORDER_E_SPLIT_DELIVERY (8 returnable units, ample headroom), and asserts the new number matches the FULL pattern QATESTyyMMdd-NNNNN -- prefix AND date AND zero-padded sequence -- because a case that only checked the prefix would still pass a template engine that broke the {0:yyMMdd}/{1:D5} format tokens themselves. There is no GraphQL field exposing the raw template string, so the ONLY way to prove restoration is to create a SECOND throwaway Draft after restoring the setting and confirm its number reverts to the RET prefix; both throwaway returns are cancelled inline. createReturn is a MUTATION, so it cannot be polled (every retry would persist another Draft): the case writes the template, RESETS THE PLATFORM CACHE, then creates exactly once - the reset replaces the former fixed 60 s wait, which was not enough (run REG-2026-10-01-2133 still got the RET prefix). Written through POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings/v2/tenant/Store/{{STORE_ID}}/values (flat {settingName: value} body; a PUT /api/stores would replace the WHOLE store entity and is never used). CACHE: a store-setting write is NOT visible to xAPI until the platform cache is reset - MEASURED LIVE 2026-10-01 on vcptcore-qa1: the write returned 204 and returnPolicy kept the old value for 9+ minutes (run REG-2026-10-01-2133), while POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform-cache/reset (204, no body; the call behind Admin Settings -> Reset cache, taken from the platform Swagger) made the very next read current. So EVERY write below is followed by that reset and the short [WAIT until] poll is only a safety net. Cleanup restores the setting AND resets the cache.

[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT]
[REST-OP set_template]
POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings/v2/tenant/Store/{{STORE_ID}}/values
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"Return.ReturnNewNumberTemplate": "QATEST{0:yyMMdd}-{1:D5}"}
[REST-EXEC set_template]
[REST-OP reset_set_template]
POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform-cache/reset
[REST-EXEC reset_set_template]
[AUTH role=USER]
[GQL-OP create_new_template]
mutation { createReturn(command: { orderId: "@td(RETURNS_ORDER_E_SPLIT_DELIVERY.id)", items: [{ orderLineItemId: "@td(RETURNS_ORDER_E_SPLIT_DELIVERY.lineXItemId)", quantity: 1 }] }) { id number status } }
[GQL-EXEC create_new_template]
[GQL-CAPTURE create_new_template.data.createReturn.id → NEW_TEMPLATE_RETURN_ID]
[GQL-OP cancel_new_template]
mutation { cancelReturn(command: { returnId: "{{NEW_TEMPLATE_RETURN_ID}}" }) { id status } }
[GQL-EXEC cancel_new_template]
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT]
[REST-OP restore_template]
POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings/v2/tenant/Store/{{STORE_ID}}/values
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"Return.ReturnNewNumberTemplate": "RET{0:yyMMdd}-{1:D5}"}
[REST-EXEC restore_template]
[REST-OP reset_restore_template]
POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform-cache/reset
[REST-EXEC reset_restore_template]
[AUTH role=USER]
[GQL-OP create_restored_template]
mutation { createReturn(command: { orderId: "@td(RETURNS_ORDER_E_SPLIT_DELIVERY.id)", items: [{ orderLineItemId: "@td(RETURNS_ORDER_E_SPLIT_DELIVERY.lineXItemId)", quantity: 1 }] }) { id number status } }

Title: returnReasons -- localizedName Is Per-Culture Admin Text With Code Fallback, Not A Single Global String
Preconditions: Runner-native. No browser. RET-GQL-010 asserted only en-US, where D4 (the domain map's own finding) reported EVERY code's localizedName byte-identical to its code -- indistinguishable from a lookup that always falls back, never actually translating anything. Two translations were since entered into the admin dictionary specifically to break that ambiguity, and are now deliberate, durable fixture state this case relies on: FaultyOnArrival has an en-US entry ("Faulty on arrival") and a ru-RU entry ("Брак при получении"), but nothing entered for de-DE. This case queries all THREE cultures for the SAME code in one pass and asserts a genuine three-way contrast -- translated / translated DIFFERENTLY in another culture / falls back to the bare code where nothing was entered -- which a hardcoded-string lookup cannot produce (it would return the SAME text regardless of cultureName) and a lookup that always falls back cannot produce either (en-US and ru-RU would both just read the code). NoLongerNeeded (one of the four codes with nothing entered in ANY culture) is checked in all three calls and must read as its bare code every time, confirming the fallback is per-CODE, not a global off switch. No store setting is changed by this case -- it is a pure read against existing admin dictionary state, so there is nothing to restore.
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=reasons_en] errors[] empty
[COUNT label=reasons_en] data.returnReasons.length = 5
[DATA label=reasons_en] data.returnReasons[?code=FaultyOnArrival].localizedName = Faulty on arrival
[DATA label=reasons_en] data.returnReasons[?code=NoLongerNeeded].localizedName = NoLongerNeeded
[ERRORS label=reasons_ru] errors[] empty
[DATA label=reasons_ru] data.returnReasons[?code=FaultyOnArrival].localizedName = Брак при получении
[DATA label=reasons_ru] data.returnReasons[?code=NoLongerNeeded].localizedName = NoLongerNeeded
[ERRORS label=reasons_de] errors[] empty
[DATA label=reasons_de] data.returnReasons[?code=FaultyOnArrival].localizedName = FaultyOnArrival
[DATA label=reasons_de] data.returnReasons[?code=NoLongerNeeded].localizedName = NoLongerNeeded
Cross_Layer_Checks: [EVIDENCE] FaultyOnArrival reading THREE different strings across three calls in the same case -- English text, Russian text, bare code -- is the only shape that rules out both a hardcoded global string and an always-falls-back lookup at once; NoLongerNeeded staying identical across all three confirms the fallback applies per-code, not per-culture-globally
Failure_Signals: errors[] non-empty on any of the three calls; FaultyOnArrival reads the SAME string in en-US and ru-RU (translations not actually keyed by culture); FaultyOnArrival reads its bare code in en-US or ru-RU (the entered translation was lost or never persisted -- re-check the admin dictionary before filing, since this is fixture state that could have been edited by someone else); NoLongerNeeded reads a translated string in any culture (a code that should have nothing entered started falling back to something other than its own name)
Cleanup: none -- read-only query against existing admin dictionary state, no store setting or return created
